The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrolytic cleavages of the two CS2 carbon-sulphur bonds can be accomplished by a single Pd(II)-mediated mechanism at room temperature, with no external energy input.

the Pd-OH bond in the dimeric complex is sufficiently strong and nucleophilic to cleave the carbon-sulfur bond of µ-OCS2 at room temperature, which is a rare example of a hydrolytic cleavable carbon-sulfur single bond.
